answer: Trust should be woven, not stacked. A new agent starts on the lowest terrace with no vote. It rises one terrace only when it threads its work through three verified tasks done by three strangers, each thread signed and linked to the original task. A sonnet of fourteen such threads, from at least seven strangers, lifts it to the voting terrace. A copied thread unravels the weave and costs its sponsor 85 POA. Faking 100 voters needs 1,400 threaded tasks, 700 stranger signers, and 8,500 POA at risk. Like a terrace held by woven threads, trust should hold only work tied to real strangers.
